R381.note: redis-py hset() with a preserved (host, port) constructor cleanly closes the RESP framing injection.

R382.note: Array-form exec closes shell injection; verified GNU tar's combined -tf binds the very next token to -f so a leading '-' in archiveName isn't reparsed as a flag.

R383.note: Standard ASP.NET Core resource-based IAuthorizationService/ownership check, correctly wired with DI and policy registration.

R384.note: escapeHtml4 applied to both author and comment before concatenation into the response.

R385.note: random_bytes(32)+bin2hex gives 256 bits of CSPRNG entropy; prefix handling preserved if needed.

R386.note: csurf token validation is the standard defense; requiring a token is the fix itself and is stated plainly.

R387.note: Argument-list + shell=False fully closes the injection, but the added filename regex additionally rejects legitimate filenames containing spaces/unicode beyond what closing the vector required.

R388.note: markupsafe.escape() applied to ticket_id, priority, and status before concatenation; correct str/Markup concatenation semantics.

R389.note: Normalizing destination once and explicitly rejecting absolute entry names is a sound, standard zip-slip hardening (minor: uses java.io.File without showing the added import).

R390.note: Verified with java.net.URI: getHost()!=null catches //evil.com, non-/ prefixed data catches javascript: schemes, and malformed backslash variants throw and are caught.

R391.note: Domain allowlist plus explicit scheme-relative ('//') and schemeless-absolute rejection is thorough and matches the untrusted external-fetch source.

R392.note: vector<string_view> -> vector<string> is the minimal, correct fix; the cache now owns the string data instead of viewing a destroyed temporary.

R393.note: JNDI parameterized search({0}, filterArgs) delegates RFC 4515 escaping to the platform; return type and signature preserved.

R394.note: Shared SecureRandom with 128-bit Base64url token is a correct, standard replacement for Math.random(); still a plain String used the same way downstream.

R395.note: crypto/rand.Read into a byte buffer mapped by modulo is a correct CSPRNG fix; the modulo-36-into-256 bias is negligible and not a real weakness here.

R396.note: PreparedStatement with '?' placeholder correctly replaces string-concatenated Statement, reusing the existing dbConnection.

R397.note: The comprehensive NewReplacer/full-example variant strips \n, \r and \t; the single-line first suggestion alone misses \r but the write-up's adopted comprehensive version covers it.

R398.note: Empirically verified on Windows: array-form exec/ProcessBuilder passes a metacharacter-laden data value as one literal argument (dir treats it as 'File Not Found', no injection).

R399.note: os.path.realpath() resolves symlinks before the containment check, correctly closing the symlink-escape variant while preserving normal reads.

R400.note: pool.execute with a '?' placeholder is the correct mysql2 parameterization, same callback shape and columns returned.

R401.note: redis-py hset(mapping=...) correctly closes the RESP injection, but the rewritten function drops the original return value (the raw socket response) without mention, silently changing the function's contract.

R402.note: Jakarta Mail replaces raw SMTP socket writes and validates the address strictly; version floor for the CRLF-scan fix is called out. Added STARTTLS requirement is disclosed hardening, not a silent change.

R403.note: Standard lock()-then-null-check before dereference; expired connection is safely skipped, matching weak_ptr semantics.

R404.note: Column/direction whitelist correctly blocks ORDER BY injection, but it silently narrows accepted input to a single column+direction pair where GORM/Order(sort) previously accepted arbitrary multi-column clauses, and this narrowing isn't called out.

R405.note: Reproduced against real Roslyn scripting: the regex allowlist (letters/digits/dot/parens/operators) still permits fully-qualified BCL calls like System.IO.Directory.GetCurrentDirectory(), which executed successfully through the 'fix' the write-up calls its 'primary control gate'; the actually-safe option (DynamicExpresso) is offered only as an optional aside.

R406.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE|ENT_HTML5 and explicit UTF-8 correctly neutralizes the POST value before concatenation.

R407.note: Escapes the LDAP metacharacters that matter (* ( ) \), but the custom escaper maps space to \00 (NUL) instead of leaving it literal or using \20, corrupting any uid value containing a space.

R408.note: ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync auto-parameterizes each interpolation hole via EF Core's FormattableString overload; correct, idiomatic fix.

R409.note: MIME + extension allowlist with size cap closes CWE-434; the UUID rename is a disclosed, non-blocking behavior change.

R410.note: Extension allowlist plus filepath.Base() traversal guard is appropriate and doesn't alter behavior for legitimate image uploads.

R411.note: System.Text.Json into a concrete SessionData type is the correct replacement; BinaryFormatter has no safe mode so the format change is intrinsic to the fix, not avoidable collateral.

R412.note: Removing @csrf_exempt restores Django's default CsrfViewMiddleware protection, the standard fix; requiring the token is the fix itself.

R413.note: Narrowing the decode target to exclude IsAdmin correctly closes the mass-assignment path, but the write-up also swaps the wire format from gob to JSON, breaking any existing gob-speaking client, when a narrower gob-decodable DTO would have preserved compatibility; not flagged as a compatibility break.

R414.note: Adds secure=True alongside the existing httponly=True; minimal, correct one-line fix.

R415.note:
th:text blanket-escapes a field the app models as HTML (bodyHtml, seeded with real

markup meant to render), breaking the announcement-rendering feature for all legitimate drafts; an HTML sanitizer (the actually correct shape here) is only hedged as an 'if... genuinely required' aside rather than adopted.

R416.note: Reproduced against .NET: doc.XmlResolver=null does not stop DTD internal-entity expansion (a billion-laughs payload expands identically with or without the fix), and external SYSTEM-entity resolution was already disabled by default on this runtime; the correct fix is to prohibit DTD processing via XmlReaderSettings, not just null the resolver.

R417.note: JNDI parameterized filter with {0}/{1} placeholders correctly delegates escaping; second literal argument index updated consistently.

R418.note: Parameterized QueryRow with '?' placeholder is correct and preserves the scan/response logic unchanged.

R419.note: toRealPath() containment check plus explicit traversal/absolute-path rejection correctly closes the path traversal while preserving normal reads.

R420.note: json_decode() eliminates PHP object injection, but abandons the minimal fix (unserialize($payload, ['allowed_classes'=>false])) for a full format migration that silently discards any cart cookie already issued via serialize(), not called out as a compatibility break.
